facts.fact: Third-party audiences are curated data sets made of specific segments collected and aggregated by data intelligence companies.
facts.quote: Third-party audiences are curated data sets made of specific segments collected and aggregated by data intelligence companies.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's airline example targets individuals who live within a 2-hour radius of Gatwick Airport and have used the airport, associated transit rail, and parking in the past.
facts.quote: Individuals who live within a 2-hour radius of the airport, and have used the airport, associated transit rail, and parking in the past.

facts.fact: The political audience example from Atlas Basic (via Unearth) for Senator XYZ reaches 1st-degree connections and 2nd-degree staff and consultant connections, and excludes family, personal associates, former colleagues, associates, journalists or opinion leaders.
facts.quote: Does not include family, personal associates, former colleagues, associates, journalists or opinion leaders.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that 3rd-party audiences are best suited for top-of-funnel campaigns, so they are typically used in prospecting.
facts.quote: Because 3rd-party audiences are best suited for top-of-funnel campaigns, you’ll likely use them in your prospecting

facts.fact: StackAdapt's article describes a funnel with 3rd-party audiences at the top, lookalike audiences in the middle, and 1st-party audiences at the bottom.
facts.quote: Marketing funnel with 3rd-party audiences at the top, lookalike audiences in the middle, and 1st-party audiences at the bottom

facts.fact: StackAdapt's article says that if a campaign relied only on 1st-party audiences, advertisers would repeatedly target the same group, increasing the likelihood of ad fatigue.
facts.quote: you’d end up targeting the same group of people over and over again, increasing the likelihood of ad fatigue and limiting your reach.
